claims.text: scripts/frontend/offline.sh down stops the web (Caddy) service; the app on :8081 still loads but its requests to :8080 get no answer. offline.sh up starts Caddy again; nothing in DonHang.App watches Caddy, so waiting orders go out on the next trigger.
AuthController keeps the access token in memory only; reloading the page signs the customer out (build() returns null).

QueueSync.build wires three triggers: a non-null token in authProvider via ref.listen (sign-in), the online event via listenForOnline, and app start (Future.microtask; DonHangApp listens to queueSyncProvider). The Send now FAB in QueuedOrdersScreen calls sendNow. No timer, no backoff.
listenForOnline adds a listener for the window's online event that calls sendNow; nothing in it contacts the API, so whether the API answers is found out only by sending.

QueuedOrdersScreen shows notSent, rateLimited (with the resume time when known) and signInNeeded (with a sign-in action to /login) as a StatusBanner above the signed-in customer's orders; when nobody is signed in the screen is behind the sign-in guard, so a signInNeeded set then is not seen.
sendNow returns at once when a sync is already running (state.sending) or resumeAt is in the future; with no token or no sub it sends nothing and sets signInNeeded if any order is waiting, else none.

sendNow sends only orders with status waiting whose subject equals the signed-in token's sub, in queue order (oldest first, since OrderQueue.add appends), awaiting each _send before the next and stopping at the first non-null SyncState.
_send passes the stored order.idempotencyKey to createOrder; 201 → markSent with the OrderResult (order number); ApiProblem 400 or 409 → markRejected with problem.detail and the sync continues.

createOrder throws ApiUnreachable on no answer (incl. 502/503/504), ApiProblem for other non-201. _send stops: ApiUnreachable or other status → notSent; 429 → rateLimited, resumeAt = now + Retry-After; 401 → signInNeeded, no resumeAt (a later trigger resends the same token). Order stays waiting.
ApiProblem.retryAfter is the Retry-After header parsed as an integer number of seconds, or null when the header is missing or not an integer.

At stage-3, POST /api/v1/orders with an Idempotency-Key that customer already used returns the stored order with 201; while an earlier request with that key (e.g. one that got no answer) is still being stored, a resend gets 409 (its only 409), which the app marks rejected though the order may exist.
The API answers 401 when it does not accept the request's access token.

claims.text: tokenSubject reads sub from the base64url JSON payload (middle part) of the token and does not check the signature; checking it stays the API's job.
A queued order sent with another customer's token would be placed as that customer's order, because the API takes the customer from the token.

claims.text: test/queue_sync_test.dart at stage-3 has 8 tests; flutter test ends with 'All tests passed!'. Without '&& order.subject == subject', 'sends only the signed-in customer's orders' fails with a RangeError from ScriptedApi.createOrder and the other 7 pass.
Sending queued orders one at a time is what lets a 429 or 401 stop the rest; sent in parallel, the others are already on their way.
Do not delete a queued order that got no answer: it may already exist on the server, and its stored key is the only way to get it back; resending as a new order with a new key can create a duplicate.
QueueSync uses Riverpod 3.0 Notifier APIs: ref.listen on authProvider, ref.read for one-off reads, ref.onDispose to stop listening, and assigning state to publish SyncState.
